headline: A halted weekend tape carries a still-tightening Fed, a 5% 10-year and $100 crude into an unpriced Sunday reopen, with Tail pinned at its floor
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt. Cash equities closed at 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini settled near 21:00Z, and equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, roughly six hours after the final slot in this window. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this assessment: the cash Nasdaq-100 settled at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX fell 4.08% to 14.81 and settled at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. WTI settled $100.30, down 1.58%, and Brent $103.87, a third consecutive decline after WTI reached a four-month high near $106 on Tuesday. The September 17 H.15 carries a 4.94% 10-year, a 4.67% 2-year and a 3.88% fed funds effective rate, with the 10-year ending Friday near 4.998% after trading back above 5.00% intraday. The backdrop is genuinely tense. The FOMC raised the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on September 16 by unanimous 12-0 vote, stating that inflation remains elevated and that the action supports a timelier return to the 2 percent goal. The Strait of Hormuz has been shut since March, and the Saudi East-West pipeline built to bypass it was struck on September 10 and shut the following day, with three pumping stations damaged and Aramco telling at least two European refiners they will receive no crude next month. The one materially new item dated today cuts the other way: CENTCOM's commander said in a Saturday video message that Hormuz oil and LNG shipments over the past two weeks reached a six-month high and that the primary transit lanes are clear of mines. None of this changes the Tail assessment for this window. Tail measures a price path that denies mean reversion, and a halted market has no mechanism to produce one. Friday's session was rotational rather than one-way: semiconductor equipment led sharply while software groups lagged, megacaps split four up and four down, and NYSE decliners outnumbered advancers 1,794 to 919 beneath a higher index. It was also triple witching, reported as the second-largest options expiration on record near $7 trillion notional, so those closing marks carry expiry-flow distortion and are a weaker guide to underlying structure than an ordinary settle. Tail therefore holds 5, eases to 4 through the deepest stretch of the halt, returns to 5 from 05:00Z Sunday and reaches 6 from 10:00Z as unpriced weekend exposure accumulates ahead of a reopen that lies outside this window. Stress drifts from 24 to 32, crossing into the moderate band at 20:00Z Saturday on elapsed unpriced time rather than on any new stress event, and Confidence steps from 74 to 64 as verified Friday evidence ages with nothing able to refresh it.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail ran 17-18 through Friday's dispersed, triple-witching cash session, then fell through 16, 11, 7 and 6 as trading ended and the contract settled, holding 5 across the final seventeen slots. Stress peaked at 50 in the Friday afternoon and decayed through 44, 33, 28 and 26 into the halt, bottoming at 21 for five consecutive hours before edging back to 23. Confidence held between 75 and 88, easing steadily once the halt removed any refreshing observation. Dominant mode was mixed across the cash session, turned trend-up into the close and has read normal for every hour since the weekend halt began.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, roughly six hours after the final slot here. Tail holds 5 for two hours, eases to 4 through the deepest part of the halt, returns to 5 from 05:00Z Sunday and reaches 6 from 10:00Z as untested weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of the reopen. Those steps reflect proximity and unpriced elapsed time, never observed structure. Stress drifts from 24 to 32, crossing into the moderate band at 20:00Z Saturday on staleness alone, and Confidence steps from 74 to 64 as Friday's verified evidence ages. Energy and Middle East headlines remain the most plausible weekend surprise vector in both directions: the Saudi pipeline repair timeline and Aramco's curtailed European allocations on one side, and Saturday's CENTCOM report of six-month-high Hormuz flows on the other, with the UN General Assembly week and a reported meeting with Gulf leaders as named checkpoints. Any such development would raise Stress and reopen-gap risk first, and would reach Tail only if a reopened tape genuinely refused retracement. A confirmed Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalance lifting SpaceX to a 2.82% weight takes effect Monday and is a known directional flow rather than a mean-reversion failure mechanism. The first scheduled macro test is Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs, well beyond this window.
